content.text:
This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. Breakers 52-M2 and CB-09 both trip at the same moment. Nothing else changes: no other breaker opens or closes, normally-open (N.O.) breakers stay open, and Standby generator G1 is not running and does not start. A load has power only if a path of closed breakers connects it to a running source. Which loads that were running before the event have no power afterwards? A load behind an open breaker was not running. Answer with the load tags (for example CH-2), in the order they appear on the drawing from left to right, separated by commas.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
**Sources before and after the event**

- **Utility 1 → T1 → 52-M1 (closed) → Bus 1 (SWGR-1)**: energized, and stays energized.
- **Utility 2 → T2 → 52-M2 (closed) → Bus 2 (SWGR-2)**: 52-M2 trips, so Bus 2 loses its only source.
- **G1 → 52-G1 (open)**: not running, so Bus E has no generator source.
- **52-T (N.O.)** stays open, so Bus 1 and Bus 2 are not tied.
- **52-ET (closed)** ties Bus 2 to Bus E, so Bus E was fed from Utility 2 before the event. With Bus 2 dead and G1 not running, Bus E has no source.

**Tie cables that matter**

- CB-02 (closed) runs from Bus 1 to Bus EB (EMCC-1), which stays energized.
- CB-04 (closed) runs from Bus 2 to Bus 1B (MCC-1B). With Bus 2 dead and CB-01 open, MCC-1B loses power.
- CB-09 (closed, now tripped) runs from Bus E to Bus 2B (PNL-2B). With CB-09 open and CB-05 open, Bus 2B loses power.

**Running loads checked against the event**

| Load | Feeding breaker | Path after event | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| CT-1 | CB-11 (closed) | MCC-1B, now dead | Loses power |
| PP-2 | CB-12 (closed) | MCC-1B, now dead | Loses power |
| CH-1 | CB-13 (closed) | MCC-1B, now dead | Loses power |
| EF-4 | CB-03 (closed) | Bus 1, live | Keeps power |
| AC-1 | CB-14 (closed) | Bus 2B, now dead | Loses power |
| LP-2 | CB-15 (closed) | Bus 2B, now dead | Loses power |
| DH-A | CB-16 (closed) | Bus 2B, now dead | Loses power |
| EV-1 | CB-18 (closed) | CB-06 → Bus 2, dead | Loses power |
| AHU-3 | CB-07 (closed) | Bus 2, dead | Loses power |
| BP-1 | CB-19 (closed) | Bus EB, live via CB-02 | Keeps power |
| LAB-2 | CB-20 (closed) | Bus EB, live via CB-02 | Keeps power |

Not running before the event, so excluded: CB-01 (CH-1 path is open), CB-05, CB-08 (EL-2), CB-10, CB-17 (CRAH-4).

**Left-to-right order** (by position on the drawing): CT-1, PP-2, CH-1, AC-1, LP-2, DH-A, EV-1 (x≈937), AHU-3 (x≈1053).

FINAL ANSWER: CT-1, PP-2, CH-1, AC-1, LP-2, DH-A, EV-1, AHU-3

I'm working through the one-line diagram, starting with the utility feeds: Utility 1 comes through T1 and breaker 52-M1 (closed) to Bus 1, and Utility 2 comes through T2 and 52-M2 (closed) to Bus 2. The generator breaker 52-G1 is open, so G1 isn't supplying anything right now. I'm also checking the tie breaker between the two buses, which is normally open.

Now I'm checking whether Bus 2 can still get power once 52-M2 opens. The tie breaker 52-T is open, and 52-ET is closed, but Bus E only leads back to G1 through an open breaker, so Bus 2 and Bus E would both go dead. I'm also tracing the CB-02 and CB-04 feeder lines to see whether either one provides an alternate path.

I'm tracing the feeder lines from the buses: CB-09 on Bus E runs down to Bus 2B, and CB-05 from Bus 2 also reaches Bus 2B, though it's open. I'm now checking the remaining breakers along Bus 2B to see whether any of them offer another route to power.

Now I'm checking whether Bus 1 and Bus EB stay energized: Bus 1 is fed from T1 through the closed 52-M1, and CB-02 is feeding Bus EB along the y=491 line. I'm also confirming whether CB-02 is actually closed, since the drawing's fill there is what I need to read.

I'm checking what Bus EB and Bus E still have once 52-M2 trips: Bus EB stays fed from Bus 1 through CB-02, and Bus E loses its source, so its loads like CB-08 and CB-09 can't be served.

I'm checking what Bus 1B still has once 52-M2 opens: it's fed through CB-04 from Bus 2, which will be dead, so I'm looking at whether CB-01 or another feeder keeps it energized.

I'm checking whether MCC-1B still has a source once CB-04 drops out with Bus 2 dead: its only other connection to Bus 1 runs through CB-01, which is open, so MCC-1B goes dark along with its loads CT-1, PP-2, and CH-1.

I'm checking the remaining load on Bus 2 after 52-M2 opens: CB-06 is closed and feeds CB-17, which is open, and CB-18, which is closed and serves the EV chargers. Since Bus 2 is dead, that feed goes with it, and I'm still tracing where the other loads on that branch get their power.

I'm checking what Bus 2B loses now that CB-09 is open: before the event it was fed from Bus E through CB-09, and with Bus 2 dead its loads, starting with CB-14, go dark as well.

I'm checking the loads on Bus 2B now that CB-09 has opened: AC-1, LP-2, and DH-A were all fed from Bus E through that breaker, and with Bus 2 dead as well, nothing else reaches the bus, so those loads go dark too.

Bus EB still gets power from Bus 1 through CB-02, and CB-03 keeps the exhaust fan on Bus 1 running. Since Bus E has no running loads, losing it doesn't matter here. CRAH-4 wasn't running either, because CB-17 is open. AHU-3 on CB-07 does go dead, since it depends on Bus 2.

Next I'm checking which loads lose power after the event: MCC-1B's CT-1, PP-2, and CH-1, Bus 2B's AC-1, LP-2, and DH-A, and Bus 2's EV-1 and AHU-3. Bus 1 and Bus EB stay energized, so EF-4, BP-1, and LAB-2 keep running. I still need to double-check Bus EB.

I'm sorting the loads left to right by their drawing positions, and I've got the order as CT-1, PP-2, CH-1, AC-1, LP-2, DH-A, and then EV-1 before AHU-3 since EV-1 sits at x=937 and AHU-3 at x=1053.

I'm running the final check on the load order and confirming that each breaker I'm counting is actually closed and filled.
